raw_response:
I'm 76 this year, and I've farmed these 8 mu for 50 years. I only went to primary school, but I know this land better than any book. My wife and I work it ourselves — we're only two people now, so I hire the rotary tiller and planter from the village when I need to. I keep 6 mu in wheat-maize rotation and 2 mu in cotton. That's the split that's worked for decades, and I'm not changing it.

For winter wheat on the 6 mu, I sow right after National Day. I'm using an improved variety — the same one my neighbor Li planted two years ago, and his yield went up to about 450 kg per mu. Before sowing, I spread 40 kg of compound fertilizer per mu, which is most of one bag. Then I topdress twice with urea: 15 kg per mu when the wheat turns green, and another 15 kg per mu at jointing. All together that comes to about 20 kg nitrogen, 8 kg phosphorus, and 6 kg potassium per mu. I irrigate three times from my well: winter water in November, jointing water in March, and grain-filling water in May. I spray pesticide twice — once for aphids in spring, once for rust if it shows up. I use rotary tillage before sowing because I can't handle a plough anymore. I expect 450 kg per mu if the spring doesn't dry out.

Come June, right after wheat harvest, I plant hybrid summer maize the same day or the next. No time to plough — I direct-seed with the no-till machine. I put 30 kg of compound fertilizer per mu in the row at sowing, then topdress with 20 kg urea at the big trumpet leaf stage. That's about 18 kg nitrogen, 6 kg phosphorus, and 5 kg potassium per mu. Maize needs water at tasseling and grain filling, so I irrigate twice. Two pesticide sprays for corn borer. I expect 500 kg per mu.

For cotton on my 2 mu, I plant in late April with an improved early variety. Cotton needs more potash and more medicine than grain crops. I put down 35 kg of compound fertilizer per mu as base, then topdress twice with 10 kg urea each time. That works out to 15 kg nitrogen, 6 kg phosphorus, and 8 kg potassium per mu. I irrigate three times — seedling water, flowering water, and boll water. I spray four times for bollworm; cotton always needs more protection. I do rotary tillage in spring. Last year I got 220 kg seed cotton per mu, and I hope for the same.

I use these amounts because last year's harvest was fine, and I don't gamble with the harvest. Fertilizer costs real money — every jin of urea is cash out of my pocket — but a bad year is a disaster I can't recover from. When I'm not sure, I do exactly what I did before. I also watch what my neighbors do. If the people around me are putting on a bag of urea, I do too. At my age, change is just risk I can't afford.
